findings.claim: SK hynix, the fund's largest September holding, reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 104.6155 trillion won, up 328% year over year, and operating profit of 83.3338 trillion won, an 80% operating margin.
SK hynix net income was 39.7756 trillion won in the third quarter, down 58% from 93.9226 trillion won in the second quarter, even though operating profit rose 38% quarter over quarter.

SK hynix said long-term agreements with 14 customers cover more than 50% of 2027 and 2028 production capacity, that it expects memory demand to exceed supply through 2030, and that it plans about 100 trillion won of shareholder returns in 2026, including a 14 trillion won third-quarter dividend.
SK hynix discontinued its review of a Solidigm IPO, which management had considered as a way to raise outside capital for Solidigm capacity and to lighten its own investment burden.

Samsung Electronics, the fund's second-largest holding, reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 195.3 trillion won and operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, of which the Device Solutions division contributed 147.1 trillion won of revenue and 106.5 trillion won of operating profit, while the MX and Networks businesses posted a 0.6 trillion won operating loss and the DX division a 0.8 trillion won operating loss.
findings.source_title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

findings.claim: Samsung's third-quarter capital expenditure was 29 trillion won, full-year 2026 capital expenditure is expected at about 84.4 trillion won with 76.8 trillion won in Device Solutions, and the foundry business expects its Taylor, Texas fab to begin operations in 2027.
findings.source_title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

findings.claim: Samsung's third-quarter dividend is 4,601 won per common share, or 30 trillion won in total, and the company said estimated 2026 shareholder returns are 90 to 110 trillion won, with the remaining plan to be set at a board meeting in late January 2027.
findings.source_title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

findings.claim: After the United States ended the validated end-user waiver in 2025, Samsung and SK hynix must renew licenses annually to import controlled U.S. chip equipment into China, and both told the Korea JoongAng Daily they do not plan significant further investment in their China plants.
findings.source_title: Korean manufacturers redraw China playbook as U.S. pressure escalates

findings.claim: The 30-day SEC yield was 0.96% and the 12-month trailing yield was 1.34% as of October 31, 2026, and the only distribution shown for the latest year was $2.037071 per share paid on December 19, 2025.
findings.source_title: iShares MSCI South Korea ETF product page

findings.claim: Trailing valuation is not extreme relative to the profit boom: the iShares page shows a P/E of 16.75 and a P/B of 1.81 as of November 11, 2026, but the NAV of $148.70 was 31.8% below the $218.02 52-week high listed on the same page.
findings.source_title: iShares MSCI South Korea ETF product page

upcoming_catalysts.event: Samsung board meeting to set the final 2026 shareholder-return amount and the next return policy
SK hynix expects HBM4 to exceed HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, with long-term agreements already covering more than half of 2027-2028 capacity
Samsung expects its Taylor, Texas foundry fab to begin operations in 2027
EWY pays distributions annually; the last reported payment was December 19, 2025, and no 2026 distribution was listed on the iShares schedule

policy_links.policy: End of the validated end-user waiver, so Samsung Electronics and SK hynix must renew licenses each year to bring controlled U.S. semiconductor equipment into their China plants
policy_links.bottleneck: U.S. export licenses for equipment used in China memory fabs
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The license regime caps further capacity additions at the China plants of EWY's two largest holdings. Both companies said they will maintain existing China lines but will not expand them significantly, and they are shifting new capacity to Korea, the United States and Vietnam. The article does not state a lost order or a revenue dollar amount.

key_risks.risk: At September 30, 2026, SK hynix and Samsung Electronics were 23.72% and 22.77% of the portfolio, and Samsung's third-quarter operating profit was almost entirely from semiconductors, so a memory-price reversal would hit the bulk of the fund.
The fund's three-year standard deviation was 44.03% and its equity beta was 2.05 as of October 31, 2026, and NAV on November 11, 2026 was $148.70 against a 52-week high of $218.02.
U.S. equipment-license limits stop Samsung and SK hynix from meaningfully expanding their China fabs, which still matter to supply while the memory shortage lasts.

notes: EWY is a fund, not an operating company. Share creations change shares outstanding but are not corporate dilution, so dilution_events_last_12m is empty. August 31, 2026 net assets are total assets of $29,253,894,064.63 minus liabilities of $1,531,110,604.83 on the N-PORT XML. The November 11 AUM figure is from the iShares product page and is not in the same filing as the August net assets, so the roughly $6.1 billion decline mixes market moves and any creations or redemptions; share-level flow for that window was not verified. The product page shows a year-to-date NAV figure of 51.39% in the header and 86.11% in a performance table, so no year-to-date return is used above. The 31.8% drawdown from the 52-week high is (218.02-148.70)/218.02. The 3.72 point tracking gap is 137.71 minus 133.99. No 2026 distribution had been declared on the iShares schedule. North Korea security risk and the won were not tied to a fund-specific primary source in this pass and are omitted.
